title: Holography Study
summary: A focused material study exploring layered iridescence, thin-film color shifts, and how a highly stylized surface can stay readable under controlled lighting.

gallery.alt: Supporting icon render showing controlled rim-light treatment

seo.title: Holography Study case study
seo.description: Material exploration focused on iridescence, readable highlights, and stylized surface response.

interactive.note: This study is intentionally presented as a still-image reference.

caseStudy.hook: Not every brief needs a large scene. Sometimes the fastest way to establish a visual direction is to isolate the material language and make it undeniable.
brief: This study focused on surface behavior rather than object complexity.
The intent was to develop a stylized iridescent read that could feel premium and controlled instead of noisy.

sections.title: Controlling a loud material
body: Highly chromatic materials can fall apart quickly when the hue shifts are stronger than the lighting structure. The setup here keeps the palette concentrated and the highlight paths deliberate.
That balance makes the result more useful for real design work because the material still reads as a designed choice instead of a novelty effect.

sections.title: Lighting as part of the shader
body: The lighting was tuned alongside the material rather than after it. That was important because iridescence changes meaning once the highlights move.
The final frame is less about a single technical trick and more about coordinating several subtle ones.

outcomes: A reusable reference for stylized premium surfaces
A stronger basis for future product and concept-facing shader work
